suggestions.fit: The Cairn Codex is a standalone quest/area guide whose current artifact predates this game baseline, so version-sensitive data and UI terminology may now be stale.
suggestions.goal: Keep the standalone Cairn Codex accurate and usable against the current game while preserving its localStorage migration path.

suggestions.fact: The official MO2 release page identifies v2.5.2 as the latest release and documents Qt 6/Python changes plus new third-party plugin interface capabilities.
suggestions.fit: Bethesda Plugin Info is waiting on a real MO2 live compatibility pass, so testing against the current released host is more meaningful than relying on the older beta target alone.
suggestions.goal: Prove dedicated column, tooltips, warnings, categories, drag/drop, DPI behavior, and restart persistence in a current real MO2 runtime.
suggestions.experiment: Create a two-lane live test: v2.5.2 release first, then a separately isolated forward-compatibility lane against current upstream only after release proof passes.
suggestions.risks: Theme/DPI/plugin-stack differences can hide regressions; do not weaken tests to fit host changes.
suggestions.acceptance: All promised controls and column behavior work in v2.5.2 with the full plugin stack, native drag/drop remains unchanged, and state survives restart.
suggestions.newNotable: The official MO2 release page identifies v2.5.2 as the latest release and documents Qt 6/Python changes plus new third-party plugin interface capabilities.

projectSuggestions.projectName: Bethesda Creations Version Tracker for MO2

suggestions.fact: MO2 v2.5.2 includes updated Starfield Creation handling and third-party plugin interface changes in the current official release line.
suggestions.fit: The Version Tracker exists specifically to reason about Bethesda Creations metadata/version state inside MO2, so current Creation behavior is directly relevant.
suggestions.goal: Verify migration, metadata, version/source data, conflict behavior, dedicated column interaction, and persistence in the current MO2 host.
suggestions.experiment: Build a deterministic fixture set covering legacy marker migration, Starfield Creation metadata, corrupt marker quarantine, and restart persistence on MO2 v2.5.2.
suggestions.risks: Creation metadata semantics differ by game and may evolve; avoid inferring versions from display text alone.
suggestions.acceptance: Fixtures migrate without data loss, no per-mod sidecars reappear, false conflicts remain zero, drag/drop is unaffected, and results persist after restart.
suggestions.newNotable: MO2 v2.5.2 includes updated Starfield Creation handling and third-party plugin interface changes in the current official release line.
suggestions.proposal: Build a deterministic fixture set covering legacy marker migration, Starfield Creation metadata, corrupt marker quarantine, and restart persistence on MO2 v2.5.2.

suggestions.fact: The official USVFS repository still describes the virtual filesystem as an alpha work in progress while noting it is a core MO2 component receiving real-world testing.
suggestions.fit: The Performance Accelerator changes MO2 hot paths and must not destabilize the host or filesystem virtualization, so performance wins need explicit isolation from USVFS behavior.
suggestions.goal: Improve startup/filter/drag responsiveness without recurring workers, lost state, crashes, or interference with MO2/USVFS behavior.
suggestions.experiment: Add an instrumentation-only benchmark mode that timestamps accelerator hooks and MO2 model/proxy phases while leaving USVFS untouched; compare enabled/disabled runs on the same library.
suggestions.risks: Synthetic proxy speedups can overstate real gains; instrumentation itself can perturb timings.
suggestions.acceptance: Repeated real-library runs show a statistically meaningful UI latency improvement, identical mod/file results, zero new USVFS errors, preserved viewport/separators, and clean shutdown.
suggestions.newNotable: The official USVFS repository still describes the virtual filesystem as an alpha work in progress while noting it is a core MO2 component receiving real-world testing.
suggestions.proposal: Add an instrumentation-only benchmark mode that timestamps accelerator hooks and MO2 model/proxy phases while leaving USVFS untouched; compare enabled/disabled runs on the same library.

suggestions.fact: DalekCraft2/Shimeji-Desktop is a 2026-active Shimeji-ee port to JDK 25 that explicitly targets backward compatibility while adding DPI scaling, bug fixes, Maven packaging, and Windows/macOS/Linux support.
suggestions.fit: The master desktop-pet research should track modern implementations that preserve Shimeji semantics instead of only cataloguing older forks.
suggestions.goal: Keep one verified desktop-pet research master covering current engines, compatibility approaches, host support, and reusable implementation lessons.
suggestions.experiment: Add a compatibility matrix row comparing pack/action XML behavior, DPI handling, packaging, platform support, and migration cost against the preserved Shimeji reference sources.
suggestions.risks: A newer fork can still diverge subtly from legacy behavior; Java 25 raises deployment requirements.
suggestions.acceptance: The master records exact source/revision/date, verified compatibility claims, tested pack behaviors, platform/runtime requirements, and a clear keep/adapt/reject decision without spawning a separate research file.

suggestions.proposal: Add a compatibility matrix row comparing pack/action XML behavior, DPI handling, packaging, platform support, and migration cost against the preserved Shimeji reference sources.

appSuggestions.fact: GitHub Projects supports persistent named views that preserve different filtered/sorted perspectives of the same underlying work items.
appSuggestions.proposal: Add Project Constellation Continuity Lenses: persistent views for Today, Blocked, Version Proof, Research Stale, Changed Since Last Visit, plus user-created lenses. Lenses never alter the canonical project data; they only change the working perspective.
appSuggestions.fit: The core problem is instantly finding where work stopped and what deserves attention without losing the full 63-project catalogue.
appSuggestions.goal: Make exact next actions, blockers, stale work, and changes since the last visit immediately visible while keeping all projects available.
appSuggestions.experiment: Ship built-in lenses plus one user-created lens stored in local state, and a per-project change journal watermark.
appSuggestions.risks: Too many lenses can become another navigation burden; defaults must stay small and deletable custom lenses must never delete project data.
appSuggestions.acceptance: Switching lenses changes only the visible perspective; all 63 projects remain searchable; custom lenses survive reload; Changed Since Last Visit updates after viewing; clearing a lens never changes project content.

appSuggestions.fact: Project Constellation now has complete source-controlled wiki coverage plus independently published Drive checkpoints, while the 63-record machine catalog intentionally preserves historical lineage and can lag newer project-specific evidence.
appSuggestions.proposal: Add a read-only Current Evidence Overlay to the presentation layer that labels the 63-record catalog as the preservation base, shows the newest research cursor/checkpoint, and directs project freshness review to source-controlled wiki evidence without rewriting historical recovery records.
appSuggestions.fit: This prevents stale catalog summaries from being mistaken for the newest verified project state while preserving all prior lineage.
appSuggestions.goal: Make freshness, evidence authority, and next research rotation visible without deleting or silently rewriting historical project data.
appSuggestions.experiment: Ship the overlay in v0.5.1 and verify all 63 records remain searchable, snapshot import/export still works, and historical recoveryHistory bytes remain semantically intact.
appSuggestions.risks: The overlay must not claim that wiki presence alone proves runtime behavior, and it must not overwrite user edits or project-owned verification evidence.
appSuggestions.acceptance: Exactly 63 projects remain; old recovery history remains present; the newest cursor is visible; source-controlled wiki is clearly identified as the freshness layer; no project status is promoted by presentation code.
